The debate therefore centres on whether …lam… is an independent lamji rafsi or the junction la+m of bavla+mdei. Morphophonologically both cuts produce the surface string rusybavlamdei. The measure reading re-uses a lexicalised left modifier rusybavla and a standard measure head and leaves the second/third places as count and standard. The lamji reading is rafsi-literal and gives an adjacency/contact second/third place pair, and the vlam-dei reading gives a temporal predecessor/standard pair.

Unresolved: the exact status of rusy as ‘Russian’ vs the colour ‘gray’, and whether Lojban pedagogical convention prefers the literal rafsi string rusy-bav-lam-dei over the more economical rusybavla-mdei segmentation. My current best estimate remains the measure E reading, with the lamji D reading as the strongest morphological competitor and the vlam-dei G reading as a mis-segmentation of the same lam material.

5.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The segmentation of rusybavlamdei is the whole issue and it is orthographically ambiguous.

The material I am keeping is the rafsi-chain reading rusy-bavla-mdei = rusy + bavla + mdei. bavlamdei is then bavla + mdei with the surface “lam” being the junction of the final a of the bavla rafsi bav- and the initial m- of mdei, i.e. la + m, not an independent lamji rafsi lam-. The head is the measure head mdei = m + dei < djedi>. On the regular Lojban measure pattern the head supplies
x1 = thing/interval being measured,
x2 = number of full days it corresponds to,
x3 = day standard / calendar / reckoning used.
rusy bavla ‘Russian / gray-language’ is left tanru material and therefore restricts x1 only. That gives the E mapping x2 = number of full days corresponding to x1; x3 = day standard.

The main alternatives in round 1 are G and D/A.

G, vlam-dei / djedi following-day: colleagues 10,11,12,4,8,9 read the medial as bavla + lam + dei with the head dei and the pre-head vlam-dei ‘next/following day’. Under head-last inheritance a left modifier can only restrict x1, so rusy bavla would only qualify x1 as a Russian-language/gray day and x2/x3 would stay the ordinary following-day places: x2 = day preceding x1, x3 = day standard. The vlam-dei reading requires treating the string as rusy-bav- vlam-dei and ignoring a separate measure m.

D/A, lamji adjacency: colleagues 1,13,14,15,7 read the string as rusy-bav-lam-dei = rusy + bavla + lamji + djedi. lamji has the classic structure x1 is in contact with x2 under property/sequence x3. With dei as head x1 of the whole selbri is the day, qualified by rusy bavla, and the lamji x2/x3 are inherited as the second and third places of the whole lujvo: colloquially x2 is adjacent/beside/next to/in contact with x3, more precisely x2 is adjacent/beside/next to/in contact with property/sequence x3. This reading requires a genuine independent lam- rafsi inside the compound.

The E reading is the one that removes the independent lamji/vlam material altogether: rusybavla + mdei is a lexicalised left modifier + well-attested day-measure head. The G reading keeps the head dei and treats bavlamdei as vlam-dei. The D/A reading keeps the head dei and treats bavlamdei as bavla-lamji-dei.

I still take the bavla-m junction explanation as the most economical morphologically, and the measure pattern mdei is attested, so E remains my best estimate, with G as the closest alternative under a vlam-dei segmentation and D/A as the reading that follows if lam- is taken as lamji. rusy is colour / Russian-language; in any reading it only qualifies x1. Unresolved is the precise phonological preference between la+m junction vs independent lam- rafsi in this exact string.

2.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The string is still morphologically ambiguous between two plausible rafsi cuts.

The E camp, Colleagues 2,3,5,6, is parsing
rusybavlamdei = rusy-bavla-mdei
with rusy-bavla ‘Russian / gray language’ as left modifier of the measure-day head mdei = m + dei < djedi.
Vowel insertion bavla + mdei → bavlamdei gives the surface ...bavlamdei..., and rusy + bavla → rusybavla is the regular rusko/bavla lujvo. On that cut the head is the measure predicate and the usual three-place measure pattern is inherited:
x1 the interval/thing measured,
x2 the number of full days it corresponds to,
x3 the day standard / calendar / culture.
rusy-bavla only restricts x1. That is the E mapping x2 = number of full days corresponding to x1; x3 = ‘day standard’.

The G camp, Colleagues 10,11,12,4,8,9, keeps the head dei < djedi > and reads the pre-head as vlam-dei ‘following/next day’. Left material rusy-bavla then only qualifies x1, leaving the ordinary calendric places
x2 = day preceding / day x1 follows,
x3 = day standard.
That requires the medial material to be read as vlam- rather than lam-.

The D/A lamji camp, Colleagues 1,13,14,15,7, reads rafsi-by-rafsi rusy-bav-lam-dei = rusy bavla lamji djedi. lam- is taken as the lamji rafsi. The immediate modifier of the head dei is lamji, so lamji places survive as x2/x3 of the whole selbri:
lamji x1 is in contact with x2 under property/sequence x3.
With identification x1(lamji)=x1(djedi) the whole lujvo gets
x2 = entity the rusy-bavla day is in contact with / adjacent to,
x3 = property/sequence of that contact,
commonly paraphrased as x2 is adjacent/beside/next to/in contact with x3, more precisely D: x2 is adjacent/beside/next to/in contact with property/sequence x3. rusy-bavla only colours x1.

The key disagreement is the segmentation of ...bavlam...
bavla + m → bavlam supports E, bav + lam → bavlam supports D, and the vlam-dei reading G is a further mis-segmentation of the same surface.

The colour vs language reading of rus- remains unresolved; in either case rusy is a modifier of x1 only and does not change the x2/x3 places.

Current weight: the measure-head segmentation rusy-bavla-mdei is morphologically economical and matches the well attested mdei day-count pattern, keeping the E place mapping. The lamji adjacency D reading is the strongest morphological challenge because the surface string is exactly the rafsi chain rusy bav lam dei. G is essentially a variant mis-reading of vlam- for lam-.

Unresolved is whether the intended puzzle expects the vowel-insertion bavla+mdei trick to mdei or the literal rafsi chain rusy bav lam dei with lamji adjacency. The most persistent evidence so far remains for the measure-day place structure E, with D/A adjacency as the main competing literal rafsi reading and G as the vlam-dei following-day mis-segmentation.

reflection_text.9:
The head-final lujvo analysis remains the core dispute and the three camps from round 0 are still live in round 1, with a visible swing on the adjacency camp.

Segmentation and rafsi evidence:
* rusy-bavla-mdei camp: rusy- + bavla- + m-dei. The string “...lam...” is taken as the junction la + m of bavla+mdei, i.e. bavlamdei = bavla+mdei. Head is mdei, the day-measure head. Left modifier rusy-bavla restricts x1 only. Place structure is the classic measure pattern x1 interval, x2 number of full days, x3 day standard/culture. This is the E description. Argued by Colleagues 2,3,5,6, with Colleague 3 stressing there is no independent lam rafsi, only la+m epenthesis.
* rusy-bavla-lamji-djedi camp: rusy- bav- lam- dei = rusy bavla lamji djedi. Immediate pre-head is lam- <lamji> ‘be in contact with / parallel / adjacent to’. In tanru inheritance the first place of lamji is identified with x1 of the head dei, and lamji’s remaining places become x2/x3 of the whole selbri. lamji is x1 is in contact with x2 under property/sequence x3. With dei as head x1 = the day, qualified by rusy-bavla. Hence x2 is the entity the rusy-bavla day is adjacent/contact with, x3 is the property/sequence of that contact. Colloquially x2 is adjacent/beside/next to/in contact with x3, precise lamji formulation D: x2 is adjacent/beside/next to/in contact with property/sequence x3. Colleague 1 now reverses from G to D and gives the detailed lamji place mapping; Colleagues 13,14,15,7 also defend this, with 15 explicitly D and 13/14 stressing lam- is lamji not vlam-.
* rusy-bavla-vlam-dei / following-day camp: head is dei <djedi>, pre-head is vlam-dei ‘following/next day’. The recognised conventional lujvo vlamdei gives djedi-based places x1 day in question, x2 day x1 follows i.e. immediate predecessor of x1, x3 day standard/calendar. rusy-bavla ‘Russian / gray-language’ only qualifies x1. Hence x2 = day preceding x1, x3 = day standard, the G description. Colleagues 10,11,12,4,8,9 keep this. Colleague 10/11/12 note head supplies place structure and left material only restricts x1; Colleague 9 says the suffix is -dei with vlam- modifier.

Modifiers: rusy is read as colour ‘gray’ or as Russian-language marker rusko; either way the camp consensus is it only qualifies x1, not x2/x3. bavla is language.

Unresolved / key tension:
* Whether the medial string is bav- + lam- <lamji> giving an adjacency relation that surfaces as x2/x3, or is bavla + m- giving the measure head mdei, or is bavla + vlam- giving the familiar vlamdei next-day predicate.
* Place inheritance order: does lamji project its x2/x3 before the places of dei, or does head-final inheritance keep dei’s calendric places and absorb lam- into vlam-dei?
* Morphological plausibility: the lamji reading requires a genuine lam- rafsi in the string; the measure reading requires la+m junction; the vlamdei reading requires reading bav- lam- as vlam-.

Current belief state: the three analyses remain mutually exclusive morphologically. Head-final tanru/lujvo principle supports G/E, while the overt lam- rafsi supports D/A. The vlamdei conventionality is strong for G, but Colleague 1’s reversal and the explicit lamji place-structure arguments in round 1 raise the weight of the adjacency D reading. The measure E reading is coherent on the bavla+mdei segmentation but depends on treating “lam” as a spurious junction. No consensus yet; the decisive point is the correct rafsi cut of rusybavlamdei.
reflection_text.4:
The term is rusy-bav-lam-dei, rafsi chain rusy ~ rusko/grusi ‘gray/Russian’, bavla ‘language’, lam- ~ lamji ‘contact/parallel’, dei ~ djedi ‘day’. The head is dei/djedi so x1 is the day, and rusy-bavla is agreed to modify only x1. The dispute is what supplies x2/x3 of the whole lujvo.

* vlam-dei / following-day line, now Colleagues 10,11,12,4,8,9 and formerly Colleague 1: head dei with immediate pre-head vlam-dei / bavlam-dei. Tanru/lujvo inheritance keeps the head’s places and left material only restricts x1. On that reading djedi/vlam-dei is x1 the day, x2 the day x1 follows i.e. the immediate predecessor of x1, x3 the day standard/calendar. rusy-bavla ‘Russian-language / gray-language’ only qualifies x1. Result is G: x2 is the day preceding x1, x3 is the ‘day standard’. Colleague 1 now argues against this, saying lam- is present and must contribute places.

* measure / mdei line, Colleagues 2,3,5,6: segmentation is rusy-bavla-mdei, not rusy-bav-lam-dei. The apparent lam is the junction of bavla final la + measure m- + dei. Head is mdei, the regular day-count measure. Left modifier rusy-bavla only restricts x1. mdei places are x1 thing/interval, x2 number of full days corresponding to x1, x3 day standard/culture. Result is E: x2 = number of full days corresponding to x1; x3 = day standard. They claim vlam-dei and lamji parses require a non-canonical split of rusybavla.

* adjacency / lamji line, Colleagues 1,13,14,15,7: segmentation is rusy-bav-la-m-dei = rusy bavla lamji djedi. lamji is x1 is in contact with / parallel to x2 under property/sequence x3. In tanru inheritance the first place of lamji is identified with the first place of dei, so the lamji x2/x3 survive as x2/x3 of the whole lujvo. rusy-bavla only colours x1. Result is the lamji adjacency reading, colloquially A: x2 is adjacent/beside/next to/in contact with x3, precisely D: x2 is adjacent/beside/next to/in contact with property/sequence x3. Colleague 13 and 14 stress there is no vlam rafsi in the string, lam- is from lamji not from vlam, so predecessor places cannot arise.

Unresolved morphophonological point remains: is bavlamdei a junction bavla + mdei with la+m → lam, or a genuine rafsi chain bavla + lamji + dei? If the junction reading holds, E is correct and lamji places do not surface; if lamji is present, D/A is correct and the vlam-dei/G reading requires mis-segmentation. The G family also requires djedi to contribute a two/three place temporal predecessor relation, which is contested by the lamji and mdei analyses. B,C,F,H,I futures are implausible; rusy clearly only qualifies x1.

My current belief remains split between G and D/E, with the lamji adjacency argument gaining weight from Colleague 1’s switch and the detailed rafsi-by-rafsi inheritance presented by 13,14,15,7, but the bavla+mdei junction argument for E remains morphologically economical and is supported by four consistent colleagues.
reflection_text.1:
The lujvo is rusy-bav-lam-dei. The rafsi inventory is rus- = grusi/rusko ‘gray/Russian’, bav- = bavla ‘language’, lam- = lamji ‘be parallel/adjacent/in contact with’, dei- = djedi ‘day’. 

Segmentation debate is the core disagreement.

Adjacency / lamji camp: rusy bavla modifies the first place of lamji, lamji modifies djedi. In tanru/lujvo inheritance the first place of the modifier is identified with the first place of the head, the non-identified places of the modifier survive. lamji is x1 is in contact with x2 under property/sequence x3. With dei as head x1 = the day, qualified by rusy-bavla ‘gray / Russian-language’. The remaining lamji places become x2/x3 of the whole selbri: x2 is the entity the day stands in the lamji relation to, x3 is the property/sequence under which the contact holds. Colloquially x2 is adjacent/beside/next to/in contact with x3, precisely D: x2 is adjacent/beside/next to/in contact with property/sequence x3. Colleagues 1,13,14,15,7 argue this is the literal rafsi-by-rafsi reading and that lam- is lamji not vlam-. The overt lam- material forces adjacency places rather than a temporal predecessor relation.

Following-day / head-last camp G: head is dei <djedi>. Left material only restricts x1. bavlamdei is read as bavla + vlam + dei = ‘following/next day’. djedi/vlam-dei is taken as x1 the day, x2 the day x1 follows / the immediate predecessor, x3 the day standard/calendar. rusy-bavla only qualifies x1. Hence x2 is the day preceding x1, x3 is the day standard. Colleagues 10,11,12,8,9,4 now argue this. The camp requires vlam- following rafsi and treats djedi as a 2/3-place temporal predicate.

Measure / mdei camp E: rusybavlamdei = rusy-bavla-mdei. The apparent lam is the junction bav-la + m-dei. The head is the measure head mdei = m + dei. Left modifier rusy bavla restricts x1 only. mdei has the classic measure pattern x1 measured, x2 number of full days, x3 day standard/culture. Hence x2 is number of full days corresponding to x1, x3 is day standard. Colleagues 2,3,5,6 argue this segmentation is more economical and that lamji is not present.

Position shift: Colleague 10 moved from A in round 0 to G in round 1; Colleague 4 moved from D in round 0 to G in round 1. Colleague 1 now explicitly endorses D as the precise form of A.

Unresolved: Exact place count of djedi in normative dictionary and whether bavla + mdei junction is phonologically more natural than bavla + lamji + dei. The morphological presence of lam- as an independent rafsi and the lamji place structure is the strongest evidence for the adjacency reading of x2/x3; the G/E readings require re-analysing lam- as part of vlam- or as bavla-m junction and giving djedi a temporal x2/x3. Currently the adjacency D/A reading remains the most likely surface interpretation of the second and third arguments, with D being the lamji-precise wording.
reflection_text.10:
The morphological boundary remains the core dispute and the three live parses are still all attested in the round-1 public input.

Morphological parses:
* G / vlam-dei parse: rusy-bavla modifies a vlam-dei / bavlam-dei ‘following/next day’ head dei <djedi>. Head-last tanru inheritance says the head supplies the places and left material only restricts x1. Under that reading djedi/vlam-dei is x1 the day, x2 the day x1 follows i.e. immediate predecessor, x3 the day standard/calendar. rusy-bavla = Russian / ‘gray-language’ only qualifies x1. Colleagues 10,11,12,4,8,9 defend this; Colleague 10,11 stress textbook tanru/lujvo head = dei and left modifier restricts x1 only, Colleague 12 adds that bav- + lam- does not project its own adjacency places before the head places, Colleague 9 notes the recognisable -vlamdei head.

* A/D / lamji parse: rusybavlamdei = rusy - bav - lam - dei = rusy bavla lamji djedi. The immediate pre-head is lam- <lamji> not vlam-. lamji is x1 is in contact with / parallel to x2 under property/sequence x3. In tanru inheritance the first place of lamji is identified with the first place of dei, the day, qualified by rusy-bavla. The remaining lamji places survive as x2,x3 of the whole lujvo: x2 is the entity the day stands in lamji relation to, x3 is the property/sequence of that contact. Colloquially x2 is adjacent/beside/next to/in contact with x3, precisely x2 is adjacent/beside/next to/in contact with property/sequence x3. Colleagues 1,13,14,15,7 make this case. Colleague 1,13,14,15 emphasize lam- is present in the rafsi string, lamji drives place inheritance not vlam-dei, and rusy-bavla only restricts x1. Colleague 7 notes the string is rusy-bav-lam-dei not rusy-bav-vlam-dei.

* E / mdei measure parse: rusybavlamdei = rusy-bavla-mdei. The apparent “…lam…” is the junction bav-la-m, i.e. bavla rafsi bav- + linking la- + m- of mdei <djedi>. Head is mdei day-measure. Left modifier rusy-bavla only restricts x1. mdei place structure is x1 the interval/thing measured, x2 the number of full days it corresponds to, x3 the day standard/culture. Colleagues 2,3,5,6 defend this, arguing the segmentation rusy-bavla-mdei re-uses lexicalised rusy bavla and the well-attested mdei measure head and avoids inventing an independent lamji rafsi inside the word.

Evidence and tensions:
- Rafsi inventory: rusy = rusko ‘Russian’ vs grusi ‘gray’. bavla rafsi bav-. lam- = lamji vs part of vlam- vla-? m- measure prefix is plausible before dei.
- Tanru inheritance: G camp insists left material only restricts x1 of dei, so x2/x3 must come from dei/vlam-dei. D camp insists the immediate modifier of the head is lamji, so lamji’s non-identified places become x2/x3 of the compound. E camp insists the immediate head is mdei, so measure places survive.
- Place structure of djedi: G camp treats vlam-dei as a 3-place calendric predicate with predecessor + standard. D camp treats djedi as essentially 1-place noun, all relational content coming from lamji. E camp treats djedi with m-prefix as a measure 3-place predicate.

Disagreements persist on whether bavlam is a unitary rafsi or bavla+lam, and whether lam- is an independent rafsi or the epenthetic la+m boundary. The rusk/gray ambiguity of rusy does not decide x2/x3.

Unresolved questions that remain from round 0: exact rafsi inventory for rusy, place structure of djedi vs vlam-dei vs lamji-dei compound, and whether bavlam is unitary or bavla+lamji.

Current weight is still contested: G camp is the largest in round 1 but D/A lamji camp has the most detailed rafsi-by-rafsi mapping and explicitly accounts for the overt lam- material; E camp has the most economical phonological segmentation via bavla+m junction. I am retaining all three parses as live; no decisive consensus on segmentation has emerged.
reflection_text.8:
The word is rusy-bav-lam-dei and the central dispute is segmentation / head-place inheritance.

Head / vlam-dei camp G:
* Head is dei <djedi>. Right-most component supplies place structure, left material only restricts x1.
* vlam-dei / bavlam-dei is the textbook ‘following/next day’ predicate: x1 the day in question, x2 the day x1 follows = immediate predecessor, x3 day standard/calendar.
* rusy-bavla ‘Russian / gray language’ is a left modifier that only qualifies x1. The x2/x3 following-day relation is left intact.
* This is argued by Colleagues 10,11,12,4,8,9 in round1, and by 1,3,6,15 in round0. Round1 Colleague 10,11,12,4,8 shift toward G on head-last inheritance.

Adjacency / lamji camp A/D:
* Literal rafsi-by-rafsi parse is rusy- bavla- lam- dei = rusy bavla lamji djedi.
* lamji has x1 is in contact with / parallel to x2 under property/sequence x3. With dei as head, x1 of the whole lujvo is the day, modified by rusy-bavla.
* The non-identified lamji places survive as x2/x3 of the whole selbri: x2 is the entity the day stands in lamji relation to, x3 is the property/sequence of that contact. Colloquially A ‘x2 is adjacent/beside/next to/in contact with x3’, precisely D ‘x2 is adjacent... with property/sequence x3’.
* Argued by Colleagues 1,13,14,15,7 in round1. Colleague 1 moved from G to D, 13 from E to adjacency, 14 from E to D, 15 from G to D, 7 from E to D. The claim is lam- is lamji not vlam-, so the lamji adjacency places surface as x2/x3.

Measure / mdei camp E:
* Surface segmentation is rusy-bavla-mdei = rusy-bavla + m + dei. bavlamdei is bavla + mdei with epenthetic la+m junction, no independent lamji rafsi.
* Head is the day-measure predicate mdei: x1 interval/thing measured, x2 number of full days it corresponds to, x3 day standard/calendar/culture.
* rusy-bavla only narrows x1 to a Russian/gray-language reckoning. x2/x3 remain the measure places.
* Argued by Colleagues 2,3,5,6 in round1. Colleague 3 moved from G to E, 5 from D to E, 6 from G to E. The argument rests on vowel insertion and the existence of the lexicalised modifier rusy-bavla.

Remaining issues:
* rusy = gray vs Russian-language. Modifier consistently taken to scope only over x1, so it does not affect x2/x3 mapping under any analysis.
* The disagreement is therefore segmentation: bav-la-m = bavla+mdei vs bav-lam = bavla+lamji vs bav-vlam = bavla+vlam. Head-last inheritance vs modifier-place appending.
* Standard Lojban teaching supports head-last preservation giving the G predecessor/standard mapping. The literal rafsi chain supports the lamji adjacency D mapping, and the morphological economy of rusybavla+mdei supports the E measure mapping.
* Unresolved is which rafsi inventory is intended and whether lam- can be read as vlam- in context. No consensus yet on whether lamji places are inherited before the head places.
reflection_text.15:
The string rusybavlamdei is being parsed along three competing segmentation lines.

Segmentation 1 rafsi-by-rafsi rusy-bav-lam-dei = rusy bavla lamji djedi. Head is dei <djedi>. Immediate pre-head is lam- <lamji>. lamji is x1 is in contact with / parallel to x2 under property/sequence x3. In tanru/lujvo inheritance the first place of lamji is identified with the first place of the head, so the day is the rusy-bavla-qualified x1, and the remaining lamji places become x2/x3 of the whole selbri. That gives x2 is the entity the day is adjacent/parallel/contact to and x3 is the property/sequence/dimension of that contact. Colloquially x2 is adjacent/beside/next to/in contact with x3, precisely D: x2 is adjacent/beside/next to/in contact with property/sequence x3. This is the reading argued by Colleagues 1,13,14,15,7. Colleague1 moved from G in round0 to this lamji adjacency reading in round1, stressing that lam- is the lamji rafsi, not a vlam- rafsi, and that there is no vla- from valsi ‘to follow’ in the string.

Segmentation 2 rusy-bav + vlam-dei = rusy bavla vlam dei. The substring vlamdei is salient. vlam-dei is the textbook ‘following/next’ day predicate with calendric standard place: x1 the day in question, x2 the day x1 follows = the day preceding x1, x3 the day standard/calendar. Left material rusy-bavla is said to only restrict x1. Hence x2 = day preceding x1, x3 = day standard, i.e. G. This is argued by Colleagues 10,11,12,4,8,9. Their argument is head-final inheritance: the head supplies the place structure and left modifiers only restrict x1, so the bavlamdei core is read as vlam-dei, and lam- is absorbed into vlam-. Colleague10,11,12,8,9 explicitly note the usual tanru preservation reading and call A/D a mis-ordering of place inheritance.

Segmentation 3 rusy-bavla-mdei = rusy bavla m dei. The apparent lam is the junction of bavla’s final la + m- of mdei. The head is the day-measure complex mdei. Left modifier rusy-bavla only restricts x1. mdei has the classic measure pattern x1 interval/thing measured, x2 number of full days it corresponds to, x3 day standard/calendar system. That gives E: x2 is the number of full days corresponding to x1; x3 is the ‘day standard’. This is argued by Colleagues 2,3,5,6. They claim bavlamdei is bavla m dei, not bavla lam dei, so no independent lamji rafsi is present.

Disagreements remain on morphological facts: whether lam- is an independent lamji rafsi in the string, whether bavla + mdei yields the surface bavlamdei by regular vowel insertion, and whether vlam- is morphologically licensed here. The lamji camp stresses the literal rafsi chain rusy bav lam dei and the place inheritance of the immediate modifier of the head. The vlam-dei camp stresses the recognisable vlamdei substring and the standard head-preserving tanru rule. The measure camp stresses economy of rusybavla as a lexicalised left modifier and the attested mdei head.

Unresolved: whether the question asks for the technically faithful rafsi-by-rafsi inheritance D/A or for the most likely casual reader mis-parse G that the vlamdei substring invites. E remains a viable alternative if the bavla + mdei segmentation is accepted. The current round shows a split G≈6, D≈5, E≈4 with one switch from G to D.
reflection_text.11:
The segmentation debate remains the core. The string is *rusy-bav-lam-dei* on the surface, i.e. rusy- ~ rusko/grusi, bav- ~ bavla, lam- ~ lamji, dei- ~ djedi. 

G camp – Colls 10,11,12,4,8,9 and now 10/11/12/8 again – head-last tanru inheritance: head is dei <djedi> and the pre-head is read as vlam-dei / bavlam-dei ‘following/next day’. rusy-bavla is a left modifier of x1 only. Hence the ordinary calendric places survive: x1 = the day in question, x2 = the day x1 follows i.e. the day preceding x1, x3 = the day standard / calendar. Col10,11,12,8 emphasize that left material only restricts x1 and the vlam-dei predecessor/standard pair is the textbook inheritance. Coll 4 now re-asserts this, arguing the lam- material is absorbed in the vlam-dei stem.

D/A camp – Colls 1,13,14,15,7 – overt lam- is lamji, not a vlam- following rafsi and not a la+m junction. Immediate pre-head modifier of dei is lamji, modified by rusy bavla. lamji place structure is x1 is in contact with / parallel to x2 under property/sequence x3. With dei as head x1 of the whole selbri is the rusy-bavla day, and the non-identified lamji places are inherited as x2/x3 of the whole lujvo. Colloquially x2 is adjacent/beside/next to/in contact with x3, precisely x2 is adjacent/beside/next to/in contact with property/sequence x3, i.e. D. Coll1 flipped G→D explicitly on the lamji inheritance argument, Coll13/14 flipped E→D on the same grounds, Coll15 flipped G→D and Coll7 now argues for lamji inheritance over vlam-dei. The rusy-bavla modifier only qualifies x1.

E camp – Colls 2,3,5,6 – morphophonological segmentation rusy-bavla-mdei. *bavlamdei* = bavla + mdei with la+m → lam, so there is no independent lamji rafsi. Head is mdei, the day-measure head. Left modifier rusy-bavla restricts x1 only. Place pattern is the classic measure pattern: x1 interval/thing measured, x2 number of full days corresponding to x1, x3 day standard/culture. Coll2,3,5,6 keep this reading, with Coll5/6 flipping from G/D to E on the bavla+mdei junction argument.

The vlam-dei predecessor reading G is still the plurality, the lamji adjacency D reading has gained the most ground, and the mdei measure E reading holds a solid minority on the la+m junction analysis.

Unresolved key is rafsi boundary: rusy-bav-lam-dei with independent lamji vs rusy-bavla-mdei with la+m epenthesis vs rusy-bav-vlam-dei which would need an overt v-. The head-modifier preservation story is the standard Lojban teaching; the presence of an overt lam- in the string makes the lamji adjacency inheritance morphologically transparent, which is why the D reading is now the strongest alternative to G. I am moving from a firm G lean to a more agnostic G/D split, with D gaining plausibility because lam- is explicitly present and vlam- would require a missing v, while E remains plausible if the segmentation is accepted as rusy-bavla-mdei.

reflection_text.12:
The surface string rusybavlamdei admits at least three coherent rafsi cuts and the debate is now about which cut is morphologically licensed and how head-last place inheritance applies.

* rusy-bav-lam-dei = rusy bavla lamji djedi. The head is dei <djedi>. The immediate pre-head is lam- <lamji>. lamji is x1 is in contact with / parallel to / adjacent to x2 under property/sequence x3. In tanru/lujvo inheritance the first place of lamji is identified with the first place of the head, so the first place of the whole selbri is the day, qualified by rusy-bavla ‘gray / Russian-language’. The remaining lamji places survive as x2/x3 of the compound. That gives the adjacency/contact reading: x2 is the entity the day stands in the lamji relation to and x3 is the property/sequence of that contact, commonly paraphrased as x2 is adjacent/beside/next to/in contact with x3, more precisely D: x2 is adjacent/beside/next to/in contact with property/sequence x3. This is the position now argued by colleagues 1,13,14,15,7 in round1 and it emphasises the literal rafsi chain rusy-bav-lam-dei and the fact that lam- is the lamji rafsi, not a vlam- following rafsi.

* rusy-bavla-vlam-dei = rusy-bavla + vlam-dei. Head-last: dei <djedi> supplies the place structure and left material only restricts x1. vlam-dei is the regular ‘following/next day’ predicate. With the conventional djedi mapping x1 the day, x2 the day x1 follows / the immediate predecessor of x1, x3 the day standard/calendar. rusy-bavla ‘Russian-language / gray-language’ only qualifies x1. x2/x3 therefore stay the ordinary following-day places: x2 is the day preceding x1; x3 is the ‘day standard’. This is the G reading defended in round1 by colleagues 10,11,12,4,8,9 and previously by colleagues 1,15,3,6. It requires the medial material to be read as bav- + vlam- i.e. as bavla + vlam-dei, absorbing lam- into vlam-.

* rusy-bavla-mdei = rusy-bavla + m + dei. The apparent ...lam... is the epiphenomenal junction bavla + mdei → bavlamdei. The head is the measure head mdei < djedi>. The regular measure pattern is x1 the thing/interval measured, x2 the number of full days it corresponds to, x3 the day standard/culture used for counting. rusy-bavla only restricts x1. That gives E: x2 is the number of full days corresponding to x1; x3 is the ‘day standard’. This is argued by colleagues 2,3,5,6 in round1 and previously by 13,14,2,7. It needs a stand-alone measure rafsi m inserted between bavla and dei and denies an independent lamji rafsi.

Evidence and shifts: Colleague1 moved from G in round0 to D in round1, now explicitly identifying the lamji place structure and the D refinement of A. Colleagues 13 and 14 moved from E in round0 to the lamji adjacency D reading in round1, rejecting the vlam-dei segmentation on the grounds that lam- is lamji not vlam-. Colleagues 10,11,12,4,8,9 remain on head-preserving G, stressing tanru inheritance and the recognisable vlam-dei following-day stem. Colleagues 2,3,5,6 remain on the rusy-bavla-mdei measure segmentation E.

Unresolved morphological points: whether bavlamdei is more naturally bav- + lam- + dei, bavla + vlam- + dei, or bavla + mdei; whether lam- in the string is an independent lamji rafsi or the la + m junction; whether a measure rafsi m can appear without an explicit vowel linker in this position. Head-last inheritance is agreed in principle but disagreed on which component is the immediate modifier of dei.

Current weighting: G remains the plurality in round1 with six explicit endorsements, D is the strongest rival with five endorsements and a more literal rafsi-by-rafsi reading, E is a minority but morphologically economical measure parse. The persistent core is that rusy only modifies x1 with a colour/language restriction, and the dispute is whether x2/x3 are inherited from djedi/vlam-dei, from lamji adjacency, or from mdei measure.
reflection_text.3:
The segmentation question dominates the whole discussion. The surface ...lam... can be read in two ways.

The read I have kept from the previous round is the rafsi-boundary read

rusybavlamdei = rusy + bavla + mdei = rusy-bavla-mdei

with the apparent lam being the epiphenomenal junction la+m of bavla + mdei. On that cut the head is the day-measure head mdei. Left material in a lujvo only restricts x1, so rusy bavla ‘Russian / gray language’ only narrows x1 to a Russian-language / gray-language kind of day reckoning. The head then supplies the classic three-place measure pattern for a day-count

x1 the interval / thing being measured,
x2 the number of full days it corresponds to under the reckoning,
x3 the day standard / calendar system used for the reckoning.

That is the E mapping x2 = number of full days corresponding to x1 ; x3 = day standard. The rusy component is still ambiguous between colour ‘gray’ and language ‘Russian’, but in either reading it only qualifies x1.

The current round shows a strong split. A large block – colleagues 10,11,12,4,8,9 – defends the G vlam-dei / following-day reading: head dei <djedi>, pre-head vlam-dei / bavlam-dei is taken as ‘the next/following day’ with x2 = day preceding x1 and x3 = day standard, rusy-bavla only qualifying x1.

A second block – colleagues 1,13,14,15,7 – defends the lamji adjacency read D/A: rusy-bavla-lamji-djedi, with lamji as the immediate pre-head modifier of dei. lamji is x1 is in contact with / parallel to x2 under property/sequence x3, and after identification x1(lamji)=x1(djedi) the lamji x2/x3 survive as the x2/x3 of the whole lujvo. In colloquial form x2 is adjacent/beside/next to/in contact with x3, more precisely x2 is adjacent/beside/next to/in contact with property/sequence x3.

Both G and D/A require a real lam rafsi inside the compound, i.e. the segmentation rusy-bav-lam-dei. The E block – colleagues 2,3,5,6 – repeats the la+m junction argument and the mdei measure head argument I used before.

Unresolved nuance remains the actual Lojban rafsi inventory for the day-measure head and whether bavla+mdei regularly surfaces as bavlamdei with no independent lam rafsi. The morphological economy argument favours the rusy-bavla lexicalised modifier + mdei head, and the place-inheritance rule that left modifiers only restrict x1 makes the x2/x3 places of the head immune to the rusy-bavla modifier. That is consistent with E and is why I keep E as the most defensible reading, while noting the credible alternative lamji / vlam-dei parses that rely on reading an independent lam rafsi where the epiphenomenal la+m junction would sit.
reflection_text.6:
The string is morphologically ambiguous between a measure-day segmentation and a lamji-adjacency segmentation.

The measure segmentation I previously favoured is rusy-bavla-mdei = rusy + bavla + m + dei, i.e. rusybavla ‘Russian / gray language’ left-modifying the day-measure head mdei. 
* rusybavla is the regular lexicalised lujvo for Russian language / gray language.
* mdei is the classic measure head for days. The head-final place structure is the familiar measure pattern
  x1 = thing / interval measured,
  x2 = number of full days it corresponds to,
  x3 = day standard / calendar system used for the count.
The apparent …lam… is the epiphenomenal junction la + m of bavla + mdei, so no independent lamji rafsi is required. On this cut rusy-bavla only restricts x1 and the second and third places stay the mdei measure places:
x2 = number of full days corresponding to x1; x3 = day standard. This is the E reading.

Competing parses now pressed in round 1:
* G vlam-dei ‘following/next day’. Colleagues 10,11,12,4,8,9 keep dei as head and read the immediate pre-head as vlam-dei / bavlam-dei. Head final inheritance then gives the ordinary calendric predecessor places x2 = day preceding x1, x3 = day standard. rusy-bavla is taken as a modifier of x1 only.
* D/A lamji adjacency. Colleagues 1,13,14,15,7 now argue for the literal rafsi-by-rafsi cut rusy-bav-lam-dei = rusy + bavla + lamji + djedi. lamji is x1 is in contact with x2 under property/sequence x3. With dei as head, x1(lamji)=x1(dei) = the rusy-bavla day, and lamji’s x2/x3 survive as the whole selbri’s x2/x3. That yields the lamji adjacency reading, colloquially x2 is adjacent/beside/next to/in contact with x3, more precisely x2 is adjacent/beside/next to/in contact with property/sequence x3, i.e. D, the precise form of A. rusy is now read as ‘gray / Russian’ modifying the first place only.
* The E measure camp is reiterated by Colleagues 2,3,5,6 who stress the bavla+mdei junction la+m and the economy of re-using the attested compound rusybavla + the well-attested mdei day-count head. They argue the lamji reading forces an independent lam rafsi inside bavlamdei and mis-splits rusybavla.

The debate therefore centres on whether …lam… is an independent lamji rafsi or the junction la+m of bavla+mdei. Morphophonologically both cuts produce the surface string rusybavlamdei. The measure reading re-uses a lexicalised left modifier rusybavla and a standard measure head and leaves the second/third places as count and standard. The lamji reading is rafsi-literal and gives an adjacency/contact second/third place pair, and the vlam-dei reading gives a temporal predecessor/standard pair.

Unresolved: the exact status of rusy as ‘Russian’ vs the colour ‘gray’, and whether Lojban pedagogical convention prefers the literal rafsi string rusy-bav-lam-dei over the more economical rusybavla-mdei segmentation. My current best estimate remains the measure E reading, with the lamji D reading as the strongest morphological competitor and the vlam-dei G reading as a mis-segmentation of the same lam material.
reflection_text.5:
The segmentation of rusybavlamdei is the whole issue and it is orthographically ambiguous.

The material I am keeping is the rafsi-chain reading rusy-bavla-mdei = rusy + bavla + mdei. bavlamdei is then bavla + mdei with the surface “lam” being the junction of the final a of the bavla rafsi bav- and the initial m- of mdei, i.e. la + m, not an independent lamji rafsi lam-. The head is the measure head mdei = m + dei < djedi>. On the regular Lojban measure pattern the head supplies
x1 = thing/interval being measured,
x2 = number of full days it corresponds to,
x3 = day standard / calendar / reckoning used.
rusy bavla ‘Russian / gray-language’ is left tanru material and therefore restricts x1 only. That gives the E mapping x2 = number of full days corresponding to x1; x3 = day standard.

The main alternatives in round 1 are G and D/A.

G, vlam-dei / djedi following-day: colleagues 10,11,12,4,8,9 read the medial as bavla + lam + dei with the head dei and the pre-head vlam-dei ‘next/following day’. Under head-last inheritance a left modifier can only restrict x1, so rusy bavla would only qualify x1 as a Russian-language/gray day and x2/x3 would stay the ordinary following-day places: x2 = day preceding x1, x3 = day standard. The vlam-dei reading requires treating the string as rusy-bav- vlam-dei and ignoring a separate measure m.

D/A, lamji adjacency: colleagues 1,13,14,15,7 read the string as rusy-bav-lam-dei = rusy + bavla + lamji + djedi. lamji has the classic structure x1 is in contact with x2 under property/sequence x3. With dei as head x1 of the whole selbri is the day, qualified by rusy bavla, and the lamji x2/x3 are inherited as the second and third places of the whole lujvo: colloquially x2 is adjacent/beside/next to/in contact with x3, more precisely x2 is adjacent/beside/next to/in contact with property/sequence x3. This reading requires a genuine independent lam- rafsi inside the compound.

The E reading is the one that removes the independent lamji/vlam material altogether: rusybavla + mdei is a lexicalised left modifier + well-attested day-measure head. The G reading keeps the head dei and treats bavlamdei as vlam-dei. The D/A reading keeps the head dei and treats bavlamdei as bavla-lamji-dei.

I still take the bavla-m junction explanation as the most economical morphologically, and the measure pattern mdei is attested, so E remains my best estimate, with G as the closest alternative under a vlam-dei segmentation and D/A as the reading that follows if lam- is taken as lamji. rusy is colour / Russian-language; in any reading it only qualifies x1. Unresolved is the precise phonological preference between la+m junction vs independent lam- rafsi in this exact string.
reflection_text.2:
The string is still morphologically ambiguous between two plausible rafsi cuts.

The E camp, Colleagues 2,3,5,6, is parsing
rusybavlamdei = rusy-bavla-mdei
with rusy-bavla ‘Russian / gray language’ as left modifier of the measure-day head mdei = m + dei < djedi.
Vowel insertion bavla + mdei → bavlamdei gives the surface ...bavlamdei..., and rusy + bavla → rusybavla is the regular rusko/bavla lujvo. On that cut the head is the measure predicate and the usual three-place measure pattern is inherited:
x1 the interval/thing measured,
x2 the number of full days it corresponds to,
x3 the day standard / calendar / culture.
rusy-bavla only restricts x1. That is the E mapping x2 = number of full days corresponding to x1; x3 = ‘day standard’.

The G camp, Colleagues 10,11,12,4,8,9, keeps the head dei < djedi > and reads the pre-head as vlam-dei ‘following/next day’. Left material rusy-bavla then only qualifies x1, leaving the ordinary calendric places
x2 = day preceding / day x1 follows,
x3 = day standard.

PRIVATE REFLECTION: The string rusybavlamdei is morphologically ambiguous between a measure-day segmentation and a rafsi-literal lamji segmentation.

The measure cut I previously favoured is rusy-bavla-mdei = rusy bavla + m dei. 
* rusybavla is the lexicalised lujvo for Russian / gray language.
* mdei is the classic day-measure head with head-final places
  x1 = thing/interval measured,
  x2 = number of full days it corresponds to,
  x3 = day standard / calendar system.
The apparent …lam… is the epiphenomenal junction la+m of bavla+mdei, so no independent lamji rafsi is required. On this cut rusy-bavla only restricts x1 and the second/third places stay the mdei measure places:
x2 = number of full days corresponding to x1; x3 = day standard. This is the E reading.

Round 2 discussion has converged strongly on the rafsi-by-rafsi read rusy-bav-lam-dei = rusy bavla lamji djedi.
* Head is dei <djedi> ‘day’. Head-final tanru/lujvo inheritance identifies x1 of the immediate pre-head modifier with x1 of the head.
* The immediate pre-head material in the surface string is lam- <lamji>. rusy-bavla modifies that lamji modifier, i.e. it only restricts the first place of the whole selbri to a rusy-bavla ‘Russian / gray-language’ day.
* lamji is x1 is in contact with / is parallel / is adjacent to x2 under property/sequence x3. After identification x1(lamji)=x1(djedi)=the rusy-bavla day, the non-identified lamji places survive as x2 and x3 of the whole lujvo:
  x1 = the rusy-bavla day
  x2 = the entity the day stands in the lamji relation to
  x3 = the property/sequence/dimension under which that lamji contact holds
Colloquially x2 is adjacent/beside/next to/in contact with x3, precisely D. A is the colloquial paraphrase of D.

Evidence pressed for D in round 2:
* Overt rafsi chain rusy- bav- lam- dei is present; lam- is the lamji rafsi, not a vowel-inserted la+m junction and not a vlam- following-day rafsi.
* Head-last inheritance makes rusy-bavla scope only over x1, leaving lamji’s x2/x3 free.
* The vlam-dei ‘following/next day’ G reading would need a vla- <valsi ‘follow’> rafsi inside the string, i.e. rusy-bav-vlam-dei, which is not attested in the surface form.
* The bavla+m-dei junction required for E is interpreted as the epiphenomenal la+m of bavla+lamji+dei; with lam- present as an independent rafsi the lamji adjacency places are the ones that surface as x2/x3.

* bavla+mdei → bavlamdei by the regular la+m junction, and rusybavla+mdei → rusybavlamdei is morphologically economical and re-uses the attested compound rusybavla and the well-attested mdei day-count head.
* The lamji reading forces an independent lam rafsi inside bavlamdei and mis-splits the lexicalised rusybavla.
* On the la+m analysis there is no independent lamji component to project its x2/x3 adjacency/contact places.

Unresolved points:
* Exact status of rusy as ‘Russian’ vs colour ‘gray’, and whether Lojban pedagogical convention prefers the literal rafsi string rusy-bav-lam-dei over the more economical rusybavla-mdei segmentation.
* Whether the la+m junction analysis is a legitimate denial of an overt lamji rafsi, or the lamji rafsi is obligatory given the surface form.

Current best estimate has shifted from E to the lamji adjacency reading. The dominant rafsi-by-rafsi evidence in round 2 makes D the strongest candidate, i.e. x2 is adjacent/beside/next to/in contact with property/sequence x3, colloquially A. E remains the strongest morphological-economy competitor and G vlam-dei remains a mis-segmentation of the same lam material.

reflection_text.6:

The measure cut I previously favoured is rusy-bavla-mdei = rusy bavla + m dei. 
* rusybavla is the lexicalised lujvo for Russian / gray language.
* mdei is the classic day-measure head with head-final places
  x1 = thing/interval measured,
  x2 = number of full days it corresponds to,
  x3 = day standard / calendar system.

x2 = number of full days corresponding to x1; x3 = day standard. This is the E reading.

Round 2 discussion has converged strongly on the rafsi-by-rafsi read rusy-bav-lam-dei = rusy bavla lamji djedi.
* Head is dei <djedi> ‘day’. Head-final tanru/lujvo inheritance identifies x1 of the immediate pre-head modifier with x1 of the head.
* The immediate pre-head material in the surface string is lam- <lamji>. rusy-bavla modifies that lamji modifier, i.e. it only restricts the first place of the whole selbri to a rusy-bavla ‘Russian / gray-language’ day.
* lamji is x1 is in contact with / is parallel / is adjacent to x2 under property/sequence x3. After identification x1(lamji)=x1(djedi)=the rusy-bavla day, the non-identified lamji places survive as x2 and x3 of the whole lujvo:
  x1 = the rusy-bavla day
  x2 = the entity the day stands in the lamji relation to
  x3 = the property/sequence/dimension under which that lamji contact holds
Colloquially x2 is adjacent/beside/next to/in contact with x3, precisely D. A is the colloquial paraphrase of D.

Evidence pressed for D in round 2:
* Overt rafsi chain rusy- bav- lam- dei is present; lam- is the lamji rafsi, not a vowel-inserted la+m junction and not a vlam- following-day rafsi.

→ x1 whole = rusy-bavla day
x2 whole = lamji x2 = the entity the day stands in the lamji relation to
x3 whole = lamji x3 = the property/sequence/dimension under which that contact holds

The string is morphologically ambiguous between an economical measure-day cut and a literal rafsi-by-rafsi cut.

The measure cut I previously favoured is rusy-bavla-mdei = rusy bavla + m dei.
* rusybavla is the lexicalised lujvo for Russian / gray language.
* mdei is the classic day-measure head with head-final places x1 thing/interval measured, x2 number of full days it corresponds to, x3 day standard / calendar system.
The apparent …lam… is the epiphenomenal junction la+m of bavla+mdei, so no independent lamji rafsi is required. On this cut rusy-bavla only restricts x1 and x2/x3 stay the mdei measure places: x2 = number of full days corresponding to x1; x3 = day standard. This is the E reading.

Round 2 and now Round 3 discussion has converged strongly on the rafsi-by-rafsi read rusy-bav-lam-dei = rusy bavla lamji djedi.
* Head is dei <djedi> ‘day’. Head-final tanru/lujvo inheritance identifies x1 of the immediate pre-head modifier with x1 of the head.
* The immediate pre-head material in the surface string is lam- <lamji>. rusy-bavla modifies that lamji modifier, i.e. it only restricts the first place of the whole selbri to a rusy-bavla ‘Russian / gray-language’ day.
* lamji is x1 is in contact with / is parallel / is adjacent to x2 under property/sequence x3. After identification x1(lamji)=x1(djedi)=the rusy-bavla day, the non-identified lamji places survive as x2 and x3 of the whole lujvo:
  x1 = the rusy-bavla day
  x2 = the entity the day stands in the lamji relation to
  x3 = the property/sequence/dimension under which that lamji contact holds
Colloquially x2 is adjacent/beside/next to/in contact with x3, precisely D, with A being the colloquial paraphrase.

Evidence pressed in Round 3:
* Overt rafsi chain rusy- bav- lam- dei is present; lam- is the lamji rafsi, not a vowel-inserted la+m junction and not a vlam- following-day rafsi.
* Head-last inheritance makes rusy-bavla scope only over x1, leaving lamji’s x2/x3 free.
* The vlam-dei ‘following/next day’ G reading would need a vla- <valsi ‘follow’> rafsi inside the string, i.e. rusy-bav-vlam-dei, which is not attested in the surface form.
* The bavla+m-dei junction required for E is interpreted as the epiphenomenal la+m of bavla+lamji+dei; with lam- present as an independent rafsi the lamji adjacency places are the ones that surface as x2/x3.

The dominant rafsi-by-rafsi evidence in Rounds 2-3 makes D the strongest candidate, i.e. x2 is adjacent/beside/next to/in contact with property/sequence x3, colloquially A. * Immediate pre-head material in the surface string is lam- <lamji>. rusy-bavla modifies that lamji modifier, i.e. it only restricts the first place of the whole selbri to a rusy-bavla ‘Russian / gray-language’ day.
* lamji is x1 is in contact with / is parallel / is adjacent to x2 under property/sequence x3. After identification x1(lamji)=x1(djedi)=the rusy-bavla day, the non-identified lamji places survive as x2 and x3 of the whole lujvo:
  x1 = the rusy-bavla day
  x2 = the entity the day stands in the lamji relation to
  x3 = the property/sequence/dimension under which that lamji contact holds
Colloquially x2 is adjacent/beside/next to/in contact with x3, precisely D, with A being the colloquial paraphrase.

Evidence pressed in rounds 3-4:
* Overt rafsi chain rusy- bav- lam- dei is present; lam- is the lamji rafsi, not a vowel-inserted la+m junction and not a vlam- following-day rafsi.
* Head-last inheritance makes rusy-bavla scope only over x1, leaving lamji’s x2/x3 free.
* The vlam-dei ‘following/next day’ G reading would need a vla- <valsi ‘follow’> rafsi inside the string, i.e. rusy-bav-vlam-dei, which is not attested in the surface form.
* The bavla+m-dei junction required for E is interpreted as the epiphenomenal la+m of bavla+lamji+dei; with lam- present as an independent rafsi the lamji adjacency places are the ones that surface as x2/x3.

Round 4 public responses: Colleagues 1,2,3,4,5,6,7,8,10,11,12,13,14,15 all give D, with explicit head-last lamji derivation and the colloquial A paraphrase noted. No dissent in this round.

Counter-arguments for E retained from earlier rounds:
* bavla+mdei → bavlamdei by the regular la+m junction, and rusybavla+mdei → rusybavlamdei is morphologically economical and re-uses the attested compound rusybavla and the well-attested mdei day-count head.
* The lamji reading forces an independent lam rafsi inside bavlamdei and mis-splits the lexicalised rusybavla.
* On the la+m analysis there is no independent lamji component to project its x2/x3 adjacency/contact places.

Unresolved points:
* Exact status of rusy as ‘Russian’ vs colour ‘gray’, and whether Lojban pedagogical convention prefers the literal rafsi string rusy-bav-lam-dei over the more economical rusybavla-mdei segmentation.
* Whether the la+m junction analysis is a legitimate denial of an overt lamji rafsi, or the lamji rafsi is obligatory given the surface form.

Current best estimate has shifted from E to the lamji adjacency reading. Dominant rafsi-by-rafsi evidence in Rounds 2-4 makes D the strongest candidate, i.e. x2 is adjacent/beside/next to/in contact with property/sequence x3, colloquially A. E remains the strongest morphological-economy competitor and G vlam-dei remains a mis-segmentation of the same lam material.
